sections.title: Keys: Lesson 10, Clustering and latent mixture models

keyTerms.definition: A learning task that groups data into clusters, discussed in Lesson 10.
Models with hidden variables that describe data as a mixture, covered in Lesson 10.
The instructors listed for Lesson 10 keys in the Stanford CS229 course.
The overall course title shown in the navigation for Lesson 10 keys.

recall.question: What is the title of Lesson 10 keys?
recall.answer: The title is Keys: Lesson 10, Clustering and latent mixture models.

recall.question: Who are the instructors listed for Lesson 10 keys?
recall.answer: The instructors listed are Tengyu Ma and Andrew Ng.

keyTerms.definition: An algorithm that initializes centroids, then repeats assigning points to the nearest centroid and moving centroids to the mean of their assigned points.
An optimization where each step minimizes the objective over one block of variables, so the objective is monotone non-increasing and bounded below.
An unobserved random variable in the model, such as the mixture component z^{(i)}, that is marginalized out of the likelihood.
The weights w^{(i)}_j given by p(x^{(i)}|z^{(i)}=j) phi_j divided by the sum over l of p(x^{(i)}|z^{(i)}=l) phi_l.

recall.question: Does k-means converge to a global optimum?
recall.answer: No. J is monotone non-increasing and bounded below, so it converges to a local minimum, but the parameters need not converge to a global optimum.

recall.question: How is phi_j updated in the M-step?
recall.answer: phi_j is set to the mean of the weights w_j, and mu_j and Sigma_j are updated as weighted means and covariances using those same weights.

keyTerms.definition: EM keeps probabilities while k-means keeps 0/1 decisions, and EM becomes k-means as covariance shrinks toward a scaled identity.
A cost that is lowered by assigning each point to its nearest center and minimized by the mean.
The log likelihood of the observed data under the model, tracked each iteration and asserted to increase monotonically.
Suboptimal solutions where EM or k-means can settle, handled by restarting from spread-out initializations.

recall.question: What practical safeguards does the ladder recommend when a centroid loses all its points or when solutions vary across runs?
recall.answer: Guard the division when a centroid has no points. Use multiple seeds, keep the lowest J, and report the spread across runs.

recall.question: How does EM relate to k-means in the limit of a Gaussian mixture with shrinking covariance?
recall.answer: As the covariance approaches a scaled identity with the scale shrinking toward zero, posterior responsibilities harden and EM behaves like k-means.

keyTerms.definition: Solution from setting derivative of weighted squared distance sum to zero: mu equals sum of weighted inputs divided by sum of weights.
Behavior as sigma decreases: posterior concentrates on the closest mean, producing hard assignment to the nearest centroid.
Weight assigned to data point x^{(i)} in the weighted squared distance objective.
M-step mean recomputation equivalent to k-means when assignments become hard to the nearest mu_j.

recall.question: How is the weighted mean mu derived in E07?
recall.answer: Setting the derivative of the weighted squared distance sum to zero gives mu = sum_i w_i x^{(i)} / sum_i w_i.

recall.question: What happens to the posterior responsibilities as sigma approaches zero in E08?
recall.answer: The largest exponent dominates, so the posterior concentrates on argmin_j of distance, giving hard assignment to the nearest mean. The M-step then matches the k-means centroid update.

keyTerms.definition: A Gaussian component shrinks onto one or a few points, causing its covariance determinant to approach zero.
A matrix determinant value that approaches zero when singular collapse occurs in a Gaussian component.
An optimization property that still holds even when the model becomes degenerate from singular collapse.
A fix that adds epsilon times the identity matrix to stabilize degenerate Gaussian components.

recall.question: What is a singular collapse in failure diagnosis?
recall.answer: It occurs when a Gaussian component shrinks onto one or a few points. This causes the covariance determinant to approach zero and the likelihood to approach infinity.

recall.question: What fixes are suggested for singular collapse?
recall.answer: Regularize covariances by adding epsilon I, constrain components to spherical, or use fewer components.

keyTerms.definition: A reasoning step that evaluates what would have happened under a different choice or setup.
The fictional team referenced in the counterfactual scenario for this example.
A clustering algorithm whose result from a single run depends heavily on the chosen starting seed.
The choice of the run with the highest likelihood value, used as a principled way to pick among EM restarts.

recall.question: Why is a single k-means run considered unreliable for clustering?
recall.answer: A single k-means run is treated as seed luck, meaning the result depends on the initial seed and may not be representative.

recall.question: How does EM with restarts aim to improve over a single k-means run?
recall.answer: EM with restarts explores more of the likelihood surface, and picking the highest-likelihood run offers a principled selection. Neither approach is guaranteed to reach a global optimum.

keyTerms.definition: A statement that can be tested and potentially disproved through observation or experiment.

keyTerms.term: variance of final likelihood across seeds
keyTerms.definition: The measure of how spread out the final likelihood values are when computed across different random seeds.

recall.question: What is the falsifiable claim in research question E11?
recall.answer: The claim states that as component overlap increases, the variance of final likelihood across seeds grows faster for k-means than for EM with the same restarts.

keyTerms.definition: A graph of likelihood values that changes in only one direction across its range.
The actual average values that an analysis aims to recover within a set tolerance.

recall.question: What two things verify Implementation task E12?
recall.answer: Implementation task E12 is verified by the monotone likelihood curve and by the recovery of the true means within tolerance.
